title: Police officer who shot and killed man in Parkdale cleared of wrongdoing
article: A Toronto police officer has been cleared of wrongdoing after gunning down a machete-wielding man in a Parkdale apartment last fall, the agency probing the incident said Tuesday.
The Special Investigations Unit, a provincial body that probes all such police-related deaths, announced it would not lay charges in the death of 28-year-old Amit Krishna.

The deadly confrontation happened the evening of last Oct. 23, a Saturday, when the officer and his partner went to arrest Mr. Krishna at his home, in a high-rise tenement on Dufferin Street south of King Street West.
After one of Mr. Krishna's relatives let them into the apartment, the officers woke up the young man, who was asleep in his bed, said an SIU report detailing the agency's findings.
The pair brought Mr. Krishna into the living room, explained why they were going to arrest him and then followed him back to his darkened bedroom so he could change his clothes.

The young man reached into a bag to grab some clothing, but pulled out a machete and lunged at the officer closest to him, the SIU report says. As the two struggled, Mr. Krishna struck a glancing blow with the knife, cutting him lightly on the side of the head.
The other officer pulled out his pistol and shot Mr. Krishna several times. The young man died of his injuries at the scene.

"In my view, the subject officer was justified in the use of lethal force - he saw the witness officer in immediate jeopardy of grievous injury or death as a result of the knife attack by Mr. Krishna," SIU Director Ian Scott said in a statement.

The SIU assigned five investigators and three forensics personnel to the five-month-long investigation. The probe included processing the scene of the shooting, taking photographs and video of the apartment and reviewing evidence such as five spent cartridges, the officers' handguns, their uniforms and the machete. The SIU interviewed several police officers and a number of witnesses who were in the apartment at the time, the agency said.
